<objective>
Deliver the agent-capability slice end to end: a Fleet-side named agent profile that supplies an alternate
Claude Code config directory and an explicit, strictly-scoped MCP server set, reaching a real spawn through
a forced-constant environment key and three composed argv flags — with the billing-safety contract the
phase already established left structurally untouched.

Purpose: Phase 2's argv and env builders currently foreclose all three capability channels — no
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, no MCP configuration, and an `--allowedTools` list with no `Skill` entry and no MCP
globs. That is a silent capability hole: a session runs fine and simply cannot do the things the operator
believes it can. Closing it touches the two most safety-critical functions in the codebase
(`buildWorkerEnv` and `buildSpawnArgv`), so it is proven on one thin path first, with the BILL-06 shape
test upgraded rather than weakened.

Output: `src/runner/agent-profile.ts` as the single source of profile truth, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` injected
as a Fleet-authored forced constant, `--mcp-config` structurally paired with `--strict-mcp-config`, an
`--allowedTools` value composed from the defaults plus `Skill` plus the profile's declared globs, and a
build-failing contract test for every one of those properties.
</objective>

<task type="checkpoint:decision" gate="blocking">
  <name>Task 1: One-way boundary — a repository names an agent profile, it never defines one</name>
  <decision>
Whether `.fleet.yml` — git-tracked content inside repositories Fleet does not own — may carry an agent
profile DEFINITION (an object containing MCP server entries, each of which is a `command:` plus `args:`
that Fleet would execute on the host), or may only carry a NAME that indexes into a profile defined in
Fleet's own `<FLEET_HOME>/config.json`.
  </decision>
  <context>
D-35 already selects naming-only, and this checkpoint exists to confirm that selection with the developer
before code depends on it — not to reopen it. It is gated because the reversibility rating is `one-way`:
once repositories are permitted to define profiles and real repos start relying on it, withdrawing the
capability breaks every one of them, so the decision cannot be quietly walked back the way a cap default
or a tool list can.

What is actually at stake: an MCP stdio server definition is an executable command line. Admitting one
from repository content would mean that cloning and registering any repository grants that repository
arbitrary process spawn on this machine, under the daemon's user, at every task dispatch — with no review
step between `git pull` and execution. `01-02-PLAN.md` already locked the narrower form of this rule
("MUST NOT execute anything sourced from a repo's `.fleet.yml`"), and `src/registry/fleet-yaml.ts`'s
header comment records that `setup` and `test` are read and displayed only.

Naming-only costs real convenience: a repository cannot bring its own tooling along, and adding a new
capability for a project is a two-place edit (Fleet config plus the repo's one-line name). That is the
price being paid, and it is worth stating plainly rather than discovering later.
  </context>
  <options>
    <option id="naming-only">
      <name>Repository names a Fleet-side profile (D-35 as written)</name>
      <pros>A repository can never introduce an executable command line. `.fleet.yml` gains exactly one optional string key, mirroring the existing `env_profile` pattern. The trust boundary stays exactly where `01-02-PLAN.md` put it, so no existing invariant needs re-proving.</pros>
      <cons>Capability is not portable with the repository — a fresh clone on another machine has no profile until Fleet's config defines one. Adding a capability to a project is a two-place edit.</cons>
    </option>
    <option id="repo-defined">
      <name>Repository may define a profile inline in `.fleet.yml`</name>
      <pros>Capability travels with the repository; one edit, in the place a developer would look first.</pros>
      <cons>Every registered repository gains arbitrary process spawn on the host at dispatch time, with no review step. Directly contradicts an already-locked Phase 1 rule. Not reversible once repositories depend on it.</cons>
    </option>
  </options>
  <reversibility rating="one-way">Admitting repo-authored MCP definitions later would hand every registered repository arbitrary process spawn on the host; once repositories rely on it, removing the capability breaks them, so this is not a decision that can be quietly reversed.</reversibility>
  <resume-signal>Select: naming-only (proceed as planned), or repo-defined (stop — this contradicts D-35 and 01-02's locked rule, and the phase needs replanning before any code is written).</resume-signal>
</task>

**`src/config.ts`** — export the two config-file key names as named constants so the config reader and the
profile module cannot drift: one for the profile map and one for the default profile name. Export the
`FleetConfigFile` interface (currently module-private) and declare both keys on it as `unknown`, leaving
parsing to the profile module. Do not import anything from `src/runner/` here — `config.ts` is imported by
the CLI, which is forbidden from reaching into runner internals, and a cycle would follow.

**`src/runner/agent-profile.ts`** — new module, the single source of profile truth. Open it with a doc
comment naming AGENT-01…04 and the property it defends, matching `env.ts`'s and `git-inspect.ts`'s header
convention: this module is the trust boundary between Fleet-authored configuration and executable process
definitions, and nothing it returns may originate in a registered repository.

Declare a zod schema for one MCP server definition permitting the transports Claude Code accepts — a
stdio form with a command string, an optional args string array and an optional env string map, and a
remote form with a URL and optional headers — as a discriminated union, `.strict()` on each member so an
unrecognised field fails rather than passing through. Declare `agentProfileSchema` as a `.strict()` object
with three optional fields: the Claude Code config directory as a string, the MCP servers as a record of
server name to server definition, and extra allowed tools as a string array. Declare the store schema as a
record of profile name to profile.

Export a `ResolvedAgentProfile` interface carrying the profile `name`, a `claudeConfigDir` that is a string
or null, an `mcpConfig` that is either null or an object with a single `mcpServers` field, an
`mcpToolGlobs` string array, and an `extraAllowedTools` string array. Export `MCP_TOOL_PREFIX` as the
literal `mcp__` and `SKILL_TOOL_NAME` as the literal `Skill`, and a pure `mcpToolGlobFor(serverName)`
returning the prefix, the server name, a double underscore, and a star — one function, so the naming
convention has exactly one definition.

Export `AgentProfileError` with a readonly `code` field, mirroring `RegistryError`'s shape, with the codes
`agent_profile_not_found`, `agent_profile_invalid`, `agent_profile_config_dir_missing`, and
`agent_profile_unknown_mcp_server`.

Export `loadAgentProfileStore(configFile)` — a PURE function taking the already-parsed config object, so it
is unit-testable with no filesystem — which reads the profile-map key, returns an empty record when the key
is absent, and throws `agent_profile_invalid` with the zod issue paths in the message when present but
malformed. Export `readAgentProfileStore()` as the thin impure wrapper that calls `readConfigFile()` and
hands the result to the pure function, and `readDefaultAgentProfileName()` returning the configured default
name or null.

Export `resolveAgentProfile(name, store)` returning a `ResolvedAgentProfile`. It throws
`agent_profile_not_found` naming the requested profile and listing the available names when the name is
absent from the store; throws `agent_profile_config_dir_missing` when a declared config directory does not
exist on disk or is not a directory; and throws `agent_profile_unknown_mcp_server` when any entry in the
profile's extra allowed tools begins with the MCP tool prefix but does not begin with
`mcpToolGlobFor(server)`'s prefix portion for some declared server. Test membership by constructing the
declared prefixes from the server names and checking `startsWith`, never by regex-extracting the server
segment out of the tool string — server names may themselves contain underscores, which makes extraction
ambiguous and membership-by-construction exact. `mcpToolGlobs` is built by mapping every declared server
name through `mcpToolGlobFor`; `mcpConfig` is null when zero servers are declared.

For the tracer, export `resolveDefaultAgentProfile()` returning a `ResolvedAgentProfile` or null: reads the
store and the default name, returns null when no default is configured, and otherwise resolves and
validates. The full taREDACTED_SECRET resolution order is plan `02-12`'s expansion.

**`src/runner/env.ts`** — implement D-33. Add a `claudeConfigDir` optional string to `WorkerEnvInput`.
Export a new `FLEET_AUTHORED_ENV_KEYS` readonly string array whose sole current member is the Claude Code
config-directory variable name, with a doc comment stating the invariant precisely: these are keys Fleet
SETS from its own configuration and never COPIES from a source environment, they are deliberately absent
from `CLAUDE_ENV_ALLOWLIST`, and the two collections must stay disjoint. In `buildWorkerEnv`, after the
existing forced-constants assignment and alongside it, set the config-directory key from
`input.claudeConfigDir` only, and only when that input is defined. Do not add the variable to the
allowlist, do not read it from `input.source`, and do not add a defensive delete — the key's absence from
the allowlist is what makes inheritance impossible, and a delete would be dead code implying otherwise.
Extend the module header comment to record that a Fleet-authored key is now part of the output and why that
does not weaken the allowlist-forward property.
